trial_court: Family Court, Durg, Civil Suit No. 16A/2016
case_name: Bhagdas Deshlahara Satnami vs Smt. Ahirmati Deshlahara

parties.respondent_defendant: Smt. Ahirmati Deshlahara Satnami and Master Kripank (wife and minor son)

facts_of_case: The husband filed a declaratory petition to set aside the order passed by the Family Court under Section 125 of the Cr.P.C on 31.05.2012. The respondent had earlier obtained a maintenance order. The husband claimed that the respondent's marriage with him was nullity due to her previous marriage and relationship with another man.

legal_principles.principle: The court may draw adverse inference if the best evidence is withheld.
legal_principles.held: The appellant being in possession of such important document to show the birth of child on particular date and having not filed it, the best evidence which would otherwise have been available, having withheld the court is required to draw adverse inference for holding back the best evidence.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party to prove the fact.
legal_principles.held: The appellant though stated that he has filed the card to prove the fact but it has not been placed on record which could have relevance. The appellant being in possession of such important document to show the birth of child on particular date and having not filed it, the best evidence which would otherwise have been available, having withheld the court is required to draw adverse inference for holding back the best evidence.

outcome.final_order: The trial court's judgment and decree dated 27.03.2019 were upheld, dismissing the declaratory petition.
